# endpointcentral_mac_custom_script (Resource)

A Mac custom script configuration: runs a script from the Script Repository on the computers of a workgroup, narrowed to custom groups.

Endpoint Central lets an API token create, read and delete configurations, but not change them (the console's modify call refuses OAuth tokens). **Every change therefore replaces the configuration**: a new one is created and the old one deleted, and the script runs again on every target. Use `create_before_destroy` so the targets are never without it.

Scripts cannot be uploaded through the API either: add them to the Script Repository in the console and find them with the `endpointcentral_script` data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Scripts are added to the Script Repository in the console (the API cannot
# upload them); look them up by file name.
data "endpointcentral_script" "computer_name" {
  name = "set-computer-name.sh"
}

data "endpointcentral_custom_group" "all_macs" {
  name = "All Mac machines"
}

# Runs the script once on every Mac. Any change replaces the configuration
# (Endpoint Central refuses API tokens on its modify call), so create the new
# one before the old one is deleted.
resource "endpointcentral_mac_custom_script" "computer_name" {
  name      = "set-computer-name"
  script_id = data.endpointcentral_script.computer_name.id
  arguments = "--prefix corp"
  frequency = "once"
  target = {
    workgroup_id      = "123456789"
    workgroup_name    = "WORKGROUP"
    include_group_ids = [data.endpointcentral_custom_group.all_macs.id]
  }

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Configuration name.
- `script_id` (String) ID of the script in the Script Repository, e.g. from `endpointcentral_script`.
- `target` (Attributes) Computers in a workgroup, narrowed to custom groups, e.g. `WORKGROUP` → include *All Mac machines*. Changing it replaces the configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--target))

### Optional

- `arguments` (String, Sensitive) Arguments passed to the script. Sensitive: kept out of plan output, but stored in the state and readable by anyone who can open the configuration in Endpoint Central.
- `description` (String) Configuration description.
- `frequency` (String) When the script runs: `once` (default) or `every_startup`.
- `logging` (Boolean) Keep the script's output in Endpoint Central. Default `false`.
- `retries` (Number) Retries after a failure, at the next startup or refresh. `0` disables retrying. Default 2.
- `success_exit_codes` (Set of Number) Exit codes that count as success. Default `[0]`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Configuration (collection) ID.
- `script_name` (String) File name of the script.
- `status` (String) Deployment status, e.g. `In Progress`.

<a id="nestedatt--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `target`

Required:

- `workgroup_id` (String) Workgroup ID (visible on an imported task or configuration).
- `workgroup_name` (String) Workgroup name, e.g. `WORKGROUP`. The API requires the name with the ID.

Optional:

- `exclude_group_ids` (Set of String) Custom group IDs whose computers are left out, e.g. macOS VMs.
- `include_group_ids` (Set of String) Custom group IDs whose computers are targeted.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import takes the configuration (collection) ID.
tofu import endpointcentral_mac_custom_script.computer_name 123456789012345
```
